facts.content: Patient reports difficulty breathing after a wasp or bee sting that occurred a few minutes ago.
facts.source_text: CC: Difficulty breathing after wasp/bee sting (few min ago)

facts.content: Patient has a rash with mild redness and a puncture at the sting site on the arm.
facts.source_text: Rash, mild redness, puncture at sting site (arm)

facts.content: Patient reports a mild sensation of lip and tongue swelling but no visible swelling.
facts.source_text: Mild lip/tongue swelling sensation; not visibly swollen

facts.content: Patient feels anxious and is worried the reaction may worsen.
Patient currently has no acute shortness of breath.
Patient has no history of anaphylaxis and does not have an EpiPen.
Patient reports occasional anxiety and is not on medication for it.
Patient has a history of eczema.
Patient is not taking medication for anxiety.
Patient is allergic to penicillin.
Patient has no known food or pet allergies.
Patient reports no relevant family history.
Patient works as a computer scientist, lives alone, and has a cat.
facts.source_text: SH: Computer scientist, lives alone, has a cat

facts.content: Examination shows a rash with mild erythema and a puncture mark on the arm.
facts.source_text: Rash, mild erythema, puncture mark at arm

facts.content: There is no visible swelling of the lips, tongue, or oral mucosa.
Respiratory effort and ability to talk are normal during the consultation.
No audible stridor is present.
There is no local swelling at the arm beyond a mild rash.
facts.source_text: No local swelling at arm beyond mild rash

facts.content: Assessment is a localized allergic reaction to an insect sting from a bee or wasp.
facts.source_text: 1. Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp)

facts.content: Patient is experiencing anxiety about possible progression of the allergic reaction.
Recommended an oral antihistamine such as chlorphenamine or an over-the-counter alternative.
facts.source_text: Recommend PO antihistamine (e.g., chlorphenamine or OTC alternative)

facts.content: Patient was educated about signs of anaphylaxis including lip or tongue swelling, shortness of breath, and stridor and instructed to seek urgent care if these develop.
facts.source_text: Educate regarding signs of anaphylaxis (lip/tongue swelling, SOB, stridor); instructed to seek urgent care if these develop

facts.content: Advised to observe for spreading erythema, warmth, or signs of infection, with consideration of antibiotics if these appear.
facts.source_text: Observe for spreading erythema, warmth, or signs of infection (consider abx if present)

facts.content: Plan includes providing written information on allergic reactions.
facts.source_text: Provide written info on allergic reactions

facts.content: Patient was reassured and advised to have a low threshold to reconsult if symptoms worsen or if concerned.
facts.source_text: Reassure; low threshold to reconsult if worsening or concerned
